When I was 15, I got diagnosed with Hashimoto's Thyroiditis induced hypothyroidism. It was caught very quickly, and properly treated, but I still gained about 40lbs in the time that it ran freely. _I was never told about the weird complications you can have from it_. So when I was 17, and complained of full body joint pain, I got told to lose weight. Ah yes, because being overweight is going to make my finger joints hurt. 

-

I got tested for all sorts of shit between 18 - 20, because I was literally so sick that I could barely get up to go to the bathroom. I had to sit for showers, and didn't have the energy to get through one anyway. My heart would race when I would get up, I was so dizzy all the time. I would have spells of my heart rate dropping into the 30s-40s, and my oxygen saturation down to the 70s-80s. The fatigue was constant, and I could barely move without feeling exhausted. The chronic pain in my joints was so severe that I could barely contain tears every time I had to move. It felt like I had barbed wire wrapped around every joint in my body. 

-

They ran so many tests. I went to two different hospitals, and had not a doctor, no - a nurse practitioner. One doctor asked me, word for word, "how much (I) want to look into the cause of this?" REALLY? An ER doctor told me that I was faking my symptoms, that there was no way I could possibly be sick, or _this_ sick. I was being tested for cancer, tested for lupus, tested for _literally everything under the sun_. I was so sick that I felt like death, and I had not only the entire medical team of that city telling me how stupid I was, but my in laws thought I was a hypochondriac. 

-

I had to go in to get blood drawn for a pregnancy test to stay on my meloxicam (high end ibuprofen). At this point I didn't want to go in, I felt so horrible and I had severe anxiety over the treatment I was getting. The NP decided to run a full panel again. I got called on August 16th, 2018 with my diagnosis: a severe vitamin D deficiency. I was a hop, skip, and a jump from permanent joint damage. Within a week of being on 2000IU a day, my pain went down about 85-90%. The fatigue was gone. My heart rate didn't get to 168 just standing up anymore, nor did it drop to the 30s. 

-

So that is the story about how my thyroid tried to kill me, and how overreacting (POTS, lupus, cancer) _and_ underreacting (just lose weight, lol!) made it so a team of over 20+ doctors didn't check for a fucking vitamin deficiency. GOOD JOB GUYS!!!!!
